items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I was in a four piece band up in the hole in the walls and there... Bechet and Johnny. And Dots, myself, Charlie. Charlie. Yeah, Charlie. Blind Charlie.

ctx.x: Well, I wanted to ask Emil about some of the clarinet players that you don't hear too much about now that he knows. The different ones that played with Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly and those guys way back. Not the clarinet players that would be known as reading musicians, but some of the other ones.

Well, I'll tell you something about that. The clarinet players that played with, well, I remember Lil Pills. That was the only name I knew anymore. Now they had another one that was the clarinet players that was the clarinet players that was the clarinet players. Now, the clarinet players that was from the lower coast. Then again, between time, they had another one there by the name of, let's see now what they call him. Charlie, Charlie, Charlie. Well, he was a pretty good clarinet player. That's about all I…
Like a variation. Yeah. Now, who were they again? Let's see now, Zeb?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Freddy's a clown player. Oh sure. [INTERVIEWEE] He played in the Liberty Bell.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: You know that time you cut the records with Charlie Love? ... That's right, yeah.

ctx.x: Well, in that time, you see, that was hard and usually. You see, you get a band, you take a link to a day like on a Sunday, or you catch every

band in town. You see, to have work, you have to have a band, you have to have a band, and you have to have a band. But on the Sundays, you catch them big clubs, they get on out there and they watch for the bands. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get out there and they watch, stand up and watch what band's coming along. The band gets the hot with you on one number, it's carrying your numbers. Well what you do, you go back and what you call the Red Bull,…
What else? He was playing clarinet. Clarinet. True clarinet.
